questions.question: Who among the following personalities, also associated with poetry and Music has been conferred with the Noble Prize?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following personalities, also associated with poetry and Music has been conferred with the Noble Prize?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rabindra Nath Tagore.

Key Points

  • Rabindranath Tagore was born on 7 May 1861 in Kolkata, West Bengal.
  • He was a poet, writer, playwright, composer, philosopher, social reformer and painter.
  • His penname was Bhanusingha.
    • He became in 1913 the first non-European and the first lyricist to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
    • He won Noble Prize for his book Gitanjali.
  • In 1901 Tagore moved to Santiniketan.
  • Gitanjali, The Post Office, Gora, Stray Birds, Kabuliwala are some of his very famous art works.
  • He died on 7 August, 1941 in Jorasanko Thakurbari, Kolkata.

Additional Information

  • Dwijendra Lal Ray
    • He was born on 19 July 1863, in Krishnanagar and died in 17 May, 1913, in Kolkata.
    • He was known for his plays and songs known as Dwijendrageeti or Songs of Dwijendralal.
    • He was civil servant, play writer, and musician.
  •  Bankim Chandra Chatterjee
    • ​He was born on 26 June 1838, in Kolkata, and died on 8 April 1894, in Kolkata.
    • He was an Indian poet, journalist and novelist.
    • Anandmath (1882) is one of its most famous book.​​
  • Purandar Das
    • ​Born in 1484, Araga and died on 2 January 1564, Vijaynagar. His full name was Shriniwasa Nayaka.
    • He was a Haridasa philosopher.
    • He was a composer, singer and one of the chief founding proponents of Carnatic music.

questions.question: Who among the following earned the sobriquet ‘Bharat Kokila’ from Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following earned the sobriquet ‘Bharat Kokila’ from Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sarojini Naidu.

Key Points

  • Sarojini Naidu was also known as the Bharat Kokila or the Nightingale of India.
  • She was called the Nightingale of India or Bharatiya Kokila because her poems are rich in imagery and emotions.
  • She was a poet, orator, and freedom fighter, a crusader for equality, and a lover of nature.
  • She was the vibrant and articulate voice of India at gatherings across the globe.
  • She has many firsts to her credit, including being the first Indian woman to become the President of the Indian National Congress and the first woman to become the governor of an Indian state.
  • Sarojini Naidu was a prolific poet whose volumes of poetry included The Golden Threshold (1905), The Bird of Time (1912), and her collected poems, published as The Sceptred Flute (1928) and The Feather of the Dawn (1961).​

Additional Information

Person Important points
Annie Besant
  • Annie Besant was a British social reformer, theosophist, and Indian independence leader.
  • Some of her famous literary works include - The Ancient Wisdom, An Autobiography, The Seven Principles of Man, etc.
Toru Dutt
  • Toru Dutt was a Bengali translator and poet from British India, who wrote in English and French.
  • She is among the founding figures of Indo-Anglian literature, alongside Henry Louis Vivian Derozio, Manmohan Ghose, and Sarojini Naidu.
  • Ancient Ballads and Legends of Hindustan is an unfinished volume by Toru Dutt posthumously published in 1882.
Sucheta Kriplani
  • Sucheta Kriplani was born on June 25, 1908.She joined the freedom struggle after completing her graduation and
    became a disciple of Gandhiji.
  • She also laid the foundation of the Women's wing of Congress in 1940.
  • She handled underground non-violent political activities during the freedom struggle.
  • She was appointed a member of the constituent assembly in 1946.
  • She sang Vande Mataram on 14th August 1947 in the opening session of parliament.
  • But due to ideological differences with Nehru, she along with her husband left congress after Independence.
  • She formed a new party of her called Kisan Majdoor Praja Party and served as MP from New Delhi.
  • But in 1957 she rejoined the congress and in 1963 became the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: The birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi is celebrated as the national festival of India. In which of the following years was Gandhi Ji born?
questions.questionHtml: The birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi is celebrated as the national festival of India. In which of the following years was Gandhi Ji born?
questions.solution: Mahatma Gandhi, born on 2nd October 1869, is celebrated as the Father of the Nation in India. India honors his birth anniversary as a national festival, Gandhi Jayanti, on 2nd October, which is also the International Day of Non-Violence. questions.question: Who among the following was the first Indian swimmer to swim across the English Channel in 1958?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was the first Indian swimmer to swim across the English Channel in 1958?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mihir Sen.

Key Points

  • Mihir Sen, a well-known long-distance and channel swimmer, traversed the 23 km-long Palk Strait, a constricting body of water connecting Tamil Nadu and the Jaffna District in Sri Lanka's Northern Province. In1966, he achieved the feat.
  • He swam from Dover to Calais in the English Channel for the first time as an Asian in 1958, a few years earlier.
  • He traveled the trip in 14 hours and 45 minutes.
  • He was the only man to cross all five continents' oceans in a single year. Dardanelles, Bosphorus, Gibralta, Palk Strait, and the full length of the Panama Canal were among the accomplishments.
  • He was listed as the "world's greatest long-distance swimmer" in The Guinness Book of Records for this extraordinary feat.
  • In 1959 he was conferred with the Padma Shri and the Padma Bhushan followed in 1967.

Additional Information

  • Shamsher Khan:
    • He was an Indian swimmer who represented his nation in the 1956 Olympics.
    • He established a national record in the 200-meter butterfly competition in 1954. He broke the previous national record at the national meet in Bangalore in 1955.
  • Brojen Das:
    • He was a Bangladeshi swimmer and the first person in his race to complete six consecutive crossings of the English Channel.
  • Virdhawal Khade:
    • He is an Indian swimmer. He competed in the men's 50, 100, and 200-meter freestyle swimming events at the Beijing Summer Olympics in 2008.
    • He established a national record for India in the 100-meter freestyle.
    • Khade won a bronze medal in the 50-meter butterfly event at the Asian Games in Guangzhou in 2010.
    • It was India's first swimming medal in 24 years at an Asian Games.

questions.question: Who is the author of the Indian national anthem?
questions.questionHtml: Who is the author of the Indian national anthem?
questions.solution: Rabindranath Tagore, the author of the Indian national anthem "Jana Gana Mana," was a distinguished poet and writer. Composed in Bengali and later translated into Hindi, the anthem was adopted on January 24, 1950, reflecting India's unity and diversity. Tagore, the first non-European Nobel laureate in Literature (1913) for his "Gitanjali" poems, founded Visva-Bharati University in Santiniketan. Born on May 7, 1861, in Kolkata, he significantly influenced Indian culture and the independence movement. Tagore also wrote the national anthem of Bangladesh, "Amar Shonar Bangla."

questions.question: who founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897?
questions.questionHtml: who founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Swami Vivekanand.
Key Points

  • Debendranath Tagore was a philosopher and social reformer who founded the Brahmo Samaj along with Keshav Chandra Sen. He also did not have any direct connection with the Ramakrishna Mission.

questions.question: Who assassinated Michael O’Dwyer, the British official responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
questions.questionHtml: Who assassinated Michael O’Dwyer, the British official responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Udham Singh.

Key Points

  • Sardar Udham Singh assassinated Michael O'Dwyer in London.
  • Udham Singh was born on December 26, 1899, in the Sangrur district of Punjab.
  • He was present at Jallianwala Bagh when Massacre took place on April 13, 1919, and was deeply moved by the mishap.
  • After that, he went to Africa to work as a labourer and from there moved to the USA.
  • In the USA, he worked with the Ghadar Party.
  • He returned to India after being called by Bhagat Singh in 1927 but was arrested here because of being involved in the activities of the Ghadar Party.
  • He was released in 1931 and went to Germany and to England in 1933.
  • On March 13, 1940, Michael O'Dwyer was attending a meeting of the East India Association and Central Asian Society, of which Udham Singh was also a part.
  • As soon as the meeting concluded, Udham Singh shot O'Dwyer dead.

Additional Information 

  • Jallianwala Bagh Massacre:
    • The incident happened in the backdrop of protests against the Rowlatt Act and the subsequent arrest of Dr. Satyapal and Saifuddin Kichlew.
    • To control the violence that emerged after the arrest of the two nationalists, restrictions were imposed on the movement of people and holding the demonstrations in Amritsar.
    • But on the day of Baisakhi, April 13, 1919, thousands of people were unaware of the restrictions gathered at Jallianwala Bagh.
    • General Dyer following the orders of Michael O'Dwyer (Lt. Governor of Punjab) directed the troops to surround the gathering and shoot the people without any warning.
    • As a result, thousands of people were killed and injured.
    • After this incident, Rabindra Nath Tagore renounced his Knighthood.
    • Mahatma Gandhi gave up the title of Kaiser-i-Hind and withdrew the Satyagrah against Rowlatt act.

questions.question: __________ is the father of the modern periodic table.
questions.questionHtml: __________ is the father of the modern periodic table.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dmitri Mendeleev.
Key Points
  • Dmitri Mendeleev was a Russian chemist who was credited with the creation of the modern periodic table.
  • He arranged the elements based on their atomic weights and properties and left gaps for the elements that had not been discovered at that time.
  • Mendeleev's periodic table was widely accepted and formed the basis for the development of the modern periodic table that we use today.
  • He also predicted the properties of some of the undiscovered elements, such as gallium and germanium, based on the patterns he observed in the periodic table.

Additional Information
  • J.J. Thomson was a British physicist who discovered the electron and isotopes, but he did not contribute to the development of the periodic table.
  • Ernest Rutherford was a New Zealand physicist who is known for his work on atomic structure and radioactivity, but he did not contribute to the development of the periodic table.
  • John Newlands was a British chemist who proposed the Law of Octaves, which states that every eighth element has similar properties. However, his work was not widely accepted and he did not contribute significantly to the development of the periodic table.

questions.question: What was the name of Swami Vivekanand’s guru?
questions.questionHtml: What was the name of Swami Vivekanand’s guru?
questions.solution: Ramakrishna Paramhansa was the spiritual guru of Swami Vivekananda, a prominent saint and mystic of 19th-century Bengal. He significantly contributed to the Indian Renaissance and the revival of Hinduism. Swami Vivekananda, originally named Narendranath Datta, was deeply influenced by Ramakrishna’s teachings and later disseminated his message globally. He introduced Indian philosophies of Vedanta and Yoga to the Western world and founded the Ramakrishna Mission, which engages in various social services.

questions.question: This legendary Indian classical flautist is known for his mastery of the bansuri (bamboo flute) and his mesmerizing performances. Who is he?
questions.questionHtml: This legendary Indian classical flautist is known for his mastery of the bansuri (bamboo flute) and his mesmerizing performances. Who is he?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Hariprasad Chaurasia.

Key Points

  •  Hariprasad Chaurasia
    • Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia was born in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, India.
    • He is an internationally acclaimed classical flautist and has significantly contributed to Indian music.
    • He has received numerous awards, including the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian award.
    • Chaurasia is known for his pioneering work in bringing the flute into the mainstream of Indian classical music.
    • He has collaborated with various international artists and has also composed music for several Bollywood films.

 Additional Information

  •  Zakir Hussain
    • Ustad Zakir Hussain is a renowned Indian tabla virtuoso, composer, percussionist, music producer, and film actor.
    • He is widely considered one of the greatest tabla players of all time. 
    • Zakir Hussain has received numerous awards, including the Padma Shri (1988), Padma Bhushan (2002), and Padma Vibhushan (2023) from the Government of India.
    • He has collaborated with many international artists like George Harrison, Mickey Hart, and John McLaughlin.
    • he was born on March 9, 1951, in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. He is the eldest son of the legendary tabla player Ustad Alla Rakha.
    • Awards: Won several Grammy Awards, including the Best Contemporary World Music Album for “Global Drum Project”.
  • Shiv Kumar Sharma
    • Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma was born on January 13, 1938, in Jammu and Kashmir India.
    • He is an Indian Santoor virtuoso who is credited with shifting the instrument from a predominantly accompaniment and ensemble role in the Sufi music of Kashmir to a solo role in the Hindustani classical music tradition of North India.
    • He has single-handedly lifted his folk instrument, the Santoor, to full acceptance within the classical solo field.
  •  Ravi Shankar
    • Ravi Shankar was an Indian musician and composer best known for popularizing the sitar and Indian classical music in Western culture.
    • He also served as director of All-India Radio.

Indian Government honours:

  • Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1962)
  • Padma Bhushan (1967)
  • Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (1975)
  • Padma Vibhushan (1981)
  • Kalidas Samman from the Government of Madhya Pradesh for 1987–88
  • Bharat Ratna (1999)

Some other important awards:

  • Ramon Magsaysay Award (1992)
  • Commander of the Legion of Honour of France (2000)
  • Honorary Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire (KBE) for "services to music" (2001)
  • UNESCO International Music Council 
  • Five Grammy Awards

questions.question: Who among the following had written the National anthem of Bangladesh 'Amar Sonar Bangla'?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following had written the National anthem of Bangladesh 'Amar Sonar Bangla'?
questions.solution: Rabindranath Tagore wrote the National Anthem of Bangladesh, "Amar Sonar Bangla," in 1905 to inspire the liberation struggle during the first partition of Bengal by Lord Curzon. The song aimed to unify Bengal and raise awareness against the communal political divide. The first ten lines of this song were adopted as Bangladesh's national anthem in 1971 during its liberation war. Tagore, a Nobel laureate in literature, also wrote the words and music for India's national anthem.

questions.question: Which great leader died due to his injuries in the Anti-Simon Commission Protest of 1928?
questions.questionHtml: Which great leader died due to his injuries in the Anti-Simon Commission Protest of 1928?
questions.solution: Lala Lajpat Rai was a prominent Indian freedom fighter and leader of the Indian National Congress. In 1928, he led a protest against the Simon Commission, a British government initiative to review the Indian constitution, which was seen as an attempt to prolong British rule. During the protest, Lala Lajpat Rai was brutally beaten by the police and sustained serious injuries. He died a few weeks later.

questions.question: In pre-independent India, who was the first person to discuss the concept of poverty line?
questions.questionHtml: In pre-independent India, who was the first person to discuss the concept of poverty line?
questions.solution: Dadabhai Naoroji was the first person to discuss the concept of poverty line in pre-independent India. He introduced the concept in his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India" published in 1901. Naoroji defined poverty line as the minimum income required to meet the basic needs of an individual.

questions.question: Who was the first speaker of the Lok Sabha after India's Independence?
questions.questionHtml: Who was the first speaker of the Lok Sabha after India's Independence?
questions.solution: Ganesh V Mavalankar was the first speaker of the Lok Sabha after India's Independence, serving from 1952 to 1956. He played a pivotal role in establishing parliamentary traditions and shaping the office of the Speaker in newly independent India. Mavalankar is often referred to as the "Father of the Lok Sabha" for his significant contributions to the legislative process. The Speaker's role is crucial in maintaining order and decorum in the House, ensuring smooth conduct of business, and making final decisions binding on all members. The Speaker also represents the House in all its powers, proceedings, and dignity.

questions.question: Which freedom fighter was involved in the Kakori Train Action in 1925, for which the British government condemned him to death?
questions.questionHtml: Which freedom fighter was involved in the Kakori Train Action in 1925, for which the British government condemned him to death?
questions.solution: Ram Prasad Bismil was the freedom fighter involved in the Kakori Train Action in 1925. The Kakori Train Action was a planned robbery of a train carrying British government funds by a group of Indian revolutionaries. The British government condemned Ram Prasad Bismil to death for his involvement in the Kakori Train Action.

questions.question: _____ is a legendary sitar player and one of India's most esteemed classical musicians.
questions.questionHtml: _____ is a legendary sitar player and one of India's most esteemed classical musicians.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Pandit Ravi Shankar.

Key Points

  •  Pandit Ravi Shankar
    • Pandit Ravi Shankar was a virtuoso sitar player and a composer who played a pivotal role in popularizing Indian classical music around the world.
    • He was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in recognition of his exceptional contribution to music.
    • Ravi Shankar collaborated with several international musicians, notably George Harrison of The Beatles, which helped introduce sitar to western audiences in the 1960s.
    • He was influential in the development of the fusion music genre, combining elements of Eastern and Western music to create unique sounds.

 Additional Information

  •  Ustad Zakir Hussain​
    • Ustad Zakir Hussain is associated with the musical instrument, Tabla.
    • He collaborated with the famous American band 'The Beatles' which deserves special mention.
    • He was designated with awards:
      • ​Padma Shri in 1988
      • Padma Bhushan in 2002
      • Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1990
      • United States National Endowment for the Arts National Heritage Fellowship, the highest award given to traditional artists and musicians by the USA.
  •  Ustad Bismillah Khan
    • Ustad Bismillah Khan used to play Shehnai.
    • Ustad Bismillah Khan (1916 – 2006) (Real name is Qamaruddin Khan), was an Indian musician credited with popularizing the Shehnai.
    • Shehnai is a musical instrument that is similar to the oboe (common in India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.)
    • He was felicitated with several awards including:
      • Padma Shri in 1961
      • Padma Bhushan in 1968
      • Padma Vibhushan in 1980
      • Bharat Ratna in 2001
    • He also played the Shehnai at the 1st Republic Day celebration in 1950.
  • Pandit Bhimsen Joshi 
    • Born on 4 February 1922 in Gadak district of Karnataka.
    • He was fond of music since childhood.
    • He was greatly influenced by Abdul Karim Khan, the founder of Kirana Gharana.
    • In 1933 he left home in search of Guru. He stayed in Bijapur, Pune and Gwalior for the next two years.
    • He also took music lessons from Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan of Gwalior.
    • He received his early education in classical music from Pandit Rambhau Kundgolkar, a disciple of Abdul Karim Khan.
    • He visited Calcutta and Punjab before returning home.
    • By 1937, Pandit Bhimsen Joshi had become a well-known khyal singer. There he also learned the nuances of khayal singing from Sawai Gandharva for many years.
    • Besides singing, he has also mastered thumri and bhajan.
    • Pandit Bhimsen Joshi passed away on 25 January 2011.
    • On 4 November 2008, he was selected for the country's highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna Award, India's highest civilian honor, which was awarded in 1975 with the Padma Bhushan in the arts.
    • Pt. Bhimsen Joshi has been awarded many honors and distinctions including Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri.

questions.question: The famous playback singer _______ is a recipient of the Bharat Ratna Award.

questions.question: Who was known as the ‘Frontier Gandhi of India’ and was the leader of North West Frontier province of British India?
questions.questionHtml: Who was known as the ‘Frontier Gandhi of India’ and was the leader of North West Frontier province of British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan.

Key Points

  • About Abdul Ghaffar Khan:
    • He was born on 6 February 1890 in Charasadda, Khyber, Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
    • Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, also known as "Frontier Gandhi", "Bachha Khan" and "Badshah Khan".
    • Abdul Ghaffar Khan was a political and spiritual leader known for his non-violent movement like Mahatma Gandhi.
    • He showed the path of non-violence to the Pathans living on the outskirts, who were always depicted as 'fighters' in history.
    • This great leader always opposed the demand for the partition of the country by the Muslim League.
    • After partition, he decided to stay with Pakistan and kept demanding an autonomous administrative unit called 'Pakhtunistan' within Pakistan.
    • He died on January 20, 1988, in Peshawar, Pakistan.

 Additional Information

  • Mahatma Gandhi
    • Mahatma Gandhi was born in the year 1869 AD.
    • Mahatma Gandhi, by name of Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, (born October 2, 1869, Porbandar, India—died January 30, 1948, Delhi).
    • He was a lawyer, politician, social activist, and writer who became the leader of the nationalist movement against the British rule of India. 
    • Indian Opinion newspaper was started by Mahatma Gandhi in South Africa.
    • In 1917, the Satyagraha movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi from Champaran to protest against the injustice done by Britishers to the indigo farmers.
  • ​​Jawaharlal Nehru
    • Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India.
    • He is the Prime Minister who has had the longest term in office.
    • He served as the prime minister of India from 15th August 1947 to 1964.
    • He is the architect of the Preamble of the Indian constitution.
    • He was the Prime Minister of India during the Indo-China war in 1962.
    • He served as the first chairman of the planning commission of India.
    • He was honored with the Bharat Ratna in 1955.
    • The name Panchayati raj was given by Jawaharlal Nehru.
    • National herald is the newspaper started by Jawaharlal Nehru.
    • He is the first prime minister to die in harness.
    • Shantivan is the cremation ground of Jawaharlal Nehru.
  • Subhash Chandra Bose
    • He founded the Independence for India League with Jawaharlal Nehru.
    • He was elected as the President of INC at its Haripura Session (1938) and Tripuri Session (1939) but resigned from Tripuri due to differences with Mahatma Gandhi.
    • He took the charge of the Indian Army (Azad Hind Fauj) in 1943 in Singapore and set up an Indian Provisional government there.
    • Subhash Chandra Bose was the one who addressed Mahatma Gandhi as the Father of the Nation.
    • He gave the famous slogans–Dilli Chalo and Jai Hind.
    • The India Struggle was his autobiography.
    • He was called Desh Nayak by Rabindranath Tagore.

questions.question: Who was the ﬁrst Chief Justice of Independent India?
questions.questionHtml: Who was the ﬁrst Chief Justice of Independent India?
questions.solution:
Option 3 is correct, i.e. Harilal J. Kania.

Harilal Jekisundas Kania was the first Chief Justice of India.

  • He was the Chief Justice of India from 14th August 1947 – 26th January 1950.
  • He read the oath of chief justice of India to Dr Rajendra Prasad(India's first President).
  • H. J. Kania served as acting editor of the Indian Law Reports.

Extra facts:

  • Mandakolathur Patanjali Sastri was the second Chief Justice of India.
  • Justice Mehr Chand Mahajan was the third Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India.
  • Sudhi Ranjan Das (S.R. Das) was the 5th Chief Justice of India.
  • Justice Uday Umesh Lalit is the current and 49th Chief Justice of India (CJI).
  • Note-
    • The President of India administers the oath of the Chief Justice(Article 124)of the Supreme Court.
    • The judge who is the senior-most in the Supreme Court is appointed as the Chief Justice.
    • In the absence of the President and the Vice-President, the Chief Justice sits as the Acting President of India.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Indian musician to receive the Grammy Life Time Achievement Award?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was the first Indian musician to receive the Grammy Life Time Achievement Award?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Pandit Ravi Shankar.
Key Points
  • Pandit Ravi Shankar, who was the first Indian musician to receive the Grammy Life Time Achievement Award in 2013.
  • Pandit Ravi Shankar was a renowned Indian sitar player and composer who introduced Indian classical music to the Western world. He collaborated with several Western musicians, including George Harrison of The Beatles, and was awarded India's highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna, in 1999.
  • Nucleya is a popular Indian electronic music producer and DJ, known for his fusion of Indian folk and classical music with bass-heavy electronic beats. He has won several awards, including the MTV Europe Music Award for Best India Act in 2016.
  • Hariprasad Chaurasia is a legendary Indian classical flautist, known for his mastery of the bansuri (bamboo flute). He has received several awards, including the Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan, two of India's highest civilian honours.
  • Ustad Zakir Hussain is a world-renowned Indian tabla player, known for his virtuosity and versatility. He has collaborated with several Western musicians, including John McLaughlin and Mickey Hart, and has won several awards, including the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan.

Additional Information

  • The Recording Academy bestows a unique Grammy Award known as the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award on "performers who, during their lifetimes, have made creative contributions of outstanding artistic significance to the field of recording."
  • This award is different from the Grammy Trustees Award, which celebrates non-performers, and the Grammy Hall of Fame Award, which honors certain records rather than individuals.
  • The first recipient of the accolade was chosen in 1963, after it was created in 1962.

questions.question: Which of the following scientists developed the Theory of Relativity?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following scientists developed the Theory of Relativity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Albert Einstein.

  • He published the first part of his theory special relativity in the German physics journal Annalen der Physik in 1905 and completed his theory of general relativity only after another decade of difficult work.

Additional Information

  •  Albert Einstein had a massive influence on contemporary physics.
    • His theory of relativity shifted the contemporary understanding of space completely.
    •  In his four papers, published in November 1915, Einstein laid the foundation of the theory.
    • In the third in particular, he used general relativity to explain the precession of the perihelion of Mercury.
    • General relativity predicted that light would bend in a gravitational field.

questions.question: Who among the following was the pioneer of widow remarriages in Maharashtra and also started a girls' school in Poona along with his wife?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was the pioneer of widow remarriages in Maharashtra and also started a girls' school in Poona along with his wife?
questions.solution: Jyotirao Govindrao Phule was a prominent social reformer from Maharashtra who significantly advanced widow remarriages and female education. Along with his wife, Savitribai Phule, he established the first girls' school in Poona (now Pune) in 1848. Phule challenged the entrenched caste system and championed the rights of oppressed groups, including women and lower castes. He founded the Satyashodhak Samaj to promote social equality and authored influential works like "Tritiya Ratna" and "Gulamgiri." Born on April 11, 1827, Phule's pioneering efforts laid the groundwork for future social reforms in Maharashtra and India.
